items.prompt: The interviewer asks: 'If an Order is deleted, what happens to its OrderLines, and how would you show that on the diagram?'
items.why: Lifecycle ownership between whole and part → composition (filled diamond) vs aggregation: a UML relationship question.

items.prompt: You need to show the order in which the booking service, seat lock, payment gateway and mailer are called, including what happens when payment times out.
items.why: Calls in time order, with an alternative branch → sequence diagram with an `alt` fragment.

items.prompt: Your diagram has `Vehicle`, `Car`, `Truck`, `Motorbike`; the interviewer asks how a new `Bus` type will get its parking fee without editing `FeeCalculator`.
items.why: 'Add a type without editing existing code' → open/closed principle (SOLID). The diagram only records the answer.

items.prompt: A student can enrol in many courses and a course has many students; neither owns the other. What should the line between them look like?
items.why: Independent lifecycles + many-to-many → plain association with `*` multiplicity on both ends (no diamond).

items.prompt: Your box diagram shows `PaymentProcessor` with a hollow-triangle dashed arrow to `«interface» PaymentMethod`, and the interviewer asks what that arrow means in code.
items.why: Dashed line + hollow triangle → realization: the class implements the interface (a notation question).

items.prompt: When drawing the diagram you notice `Report` holds a reference to `Database`, `Mailer`, `PdfRenderer` and `Scheduler`, and has 25 methods.
items.why: The diagram exposes a god class with many reasons to change → SRP (SOLID). UML just made it visible.

items.prompt: You must show that `Cart` uses a `Coupon` only as a method parameter in `apply(coupon)` and never stores it.
items.why: Temporary use without a field → dependency (dashed arrow), not association.
